scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Grida is performed to celebrate the Rabi crop harvest.

Its primary meaning is rooted in community and social harmony; it is an occasion for people from different villages to come together and celebrate their shared agricultural success through collective movement.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in three distinct chronological parts.
It begins with Sela, characterized by slow and steady footwork.
It then transitions into Selalarki, where the tempo increases and the footwork becomes energetic and fast.
Watch for Sela, Selalarki, Selabhadoni.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (_w8IwIen9IQ)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Communal gathering; dancers from different villages converge in a shared space.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The soundscape is defined by a clear shift in tempo that mirrors the three phases of the dance. It begins with a slow, deliberate pace during the Sela phase, accelerates into a high-energy rhythmic drive for Selalarki, and settles into a tempo conducive to body swaying for the final Selabhadoni section.
